title: Reset tallies: Total receipt
summary: Maintain a tally initially 0. A zero reading resets it to 0; any other reading is added to it. Record the tally after every reading. Return the sum of all values in the derived sequence; return 0 for an empty sequence.
descriptionMd:
The office tally bell resets whenever a blank separator card passes through the tray. Sol is closing the print-room account before the afternoon mail. A single total must replace the pile of working slips.

Maintain a tally initially 0. A zero reading resets it to 0; any other reading is added to it. Record the tally after every reading.

Return the sum of all values in the derived sequence; return 0 for an empty sequence.

Implement resetTalliesTotalReceipt(readings, k). k is part of the common inspection-card signature and does not affect this task's result.
unitIntro: State in a loop. Maintain a tally initially 0. A zero reading resets it to 0; any other reading is added to it. Record the tally after every reading. Keep the sequence order specified here before computing the requested receipt. A scan invariant says what has been processed and what remains. Work through the proof strip first, then change the returned summary without changing the definition of that sequence. The last card revisits loop accumulators from Hello, Keys (earlier units are used while the first two levels establish the foundations).
constraints: 1 <= k <= 8. All arithmetic results fit a signed 32-bit integer.
Numeric readings lie between -1,000,000 and 1,000,000, subject to the task's shape and ordering rules.

Target time O(n); auxiliary space including the derived sequence O(n). n is the input length; d distinct values; q query count; M maximum reading; V vertices; E edges; h tree height; r reported tree nodes.
hints: Start with state in a loop. What state describes the portion you have already processed?

Maintain a tally initially 0. A zero reading resets it to 0; any other reading is added to it. Record the tally after every reading. Derive each required reading once; do not restart the whole procedure for every output position.
Return the sum of all values in the derived sequence; return 0 for an empty sequence. Handle the empty derived sequence according to the stated return rule.

cases.explanation: The derived sequence is [7,4,11,0,12]. Return the sum of all values in the derived sequence; return 0 for an empty sequence. This gives 34.
The derived sequence is [4,8,6,10]. Return the sum of all values in the derived sequence; return 0 for an empty sequence. This gives 28.
The derived sequence is []. Return the sum of all values in the derived sequence; return 0 for an empty sequence. This gives 0.

overview: Variation: State in a loop. Build the sequence once, then report exactly what the inspection card requests.
